theater: 撒麻兒罕城與澤拉夫尚河谷

battle.name: 撒麻兒罕之戰
battle.theater: 撒麻兒罕城與澤拉夫尚河谷
battle.brief: 一二二〇年二月，成吉思汗率蒙古主力自不花剌進抵撒麻兒罕，圍城約二十日，最終以總攻破城，守軍覆滅而工匠被留下。卡面的十字弩正係此役的近射程器械：守軍靠它在城頭壓制登城者，蒙古的漢人與回回工匠則用它護住壕外作業。野戰主力始終是蒙古馬弓，弩只在城牆這一段起了作用。

kit.name: 十字弩
kit.history: 弩把射速交給了機械，代價是裝填慢。城牆上它比長弓可靠，野戰裡它比長弓脆弱。

countries: 撒麻兒罕之戰發生於一二二〇年二月，是大蒙古國第一次西征、也就是對花剌子模帝國戰役的中段戰役，交戰地點在今烏茲別克斯坦的澤拉夫尚河谷。進攻方是蒙古帝國的中央軍：成吉思汗自任大汗，親率主力並帶著幼子拖雷抵達撒麻兒罕城下，同時把大軍分作數路使用——朮赤領一軍向西北攻玉龍傑赤，察合台與窩闕台負責訛答剌方向，別兒哥帶受降的哈剌兀良哈兵掃清別失八兒與花剌子模的西北邊疆，汗王本人掌握的三萬至五萬騎才是對撒麻兒罕攻城的那一支。蒙古本部以千戶、百戶為基本編制，兵種以輕裝騎射為主，攻城所需的一切匠人則從歸附的漢人、契丹、回回與西域工匠中抽調，組成隨軍的工程隊伍，操作投石機、雲梯與撞木。防守方是花剌子模沙朝在撒麻兒罕的總督府：總督塔只丁·塔拉茲班是蘇丹穆罕默德二世倚重的藩臣之一，麾下有波斯、土耳其與突厥系的常備步騎，另有城內臨時徵召的民兵和教團武裝；全城指揮權集中在總督府與清真寺教長團體手中，防務分作內城、堡壘與沿牆各段由不同的人分段負責，缺少能統一全城作戰的指揮。蒙古軍中還有汪古等西北藩部派來的騎兵，充當前哨與斷後的耳目。
countriesEn: The siege of Samarkand was fought in February 1220, in the middle phase of the first Mongol western campaign against the Khwarazmian Empire, in the Zeravshan valley of what is now Uzbekistan. The attacking side was the central army of the Mongol Empire: Genghis Khan, who was the khan in his own right, led the main body himself and arrived before Samarkand with his youngest son Tolui, while splitting his forces into several columns. Jochi took one army northwest against Urgench, Chagatai and Ogedei were assigned to the Nishapur front, and Batu, leading the newly submitted Kara-Khitai and Oghuz auxiliaries, swept the northwest frontier of the empire in Transoxiana; the thirty to fifty thousand riders under the khan's own command were the force that actually sat down before Samarkand. The Mongol core was organised in thousands and hundreds, its weapon of choice the light horse archer, while every artisan needed for the siege was drawn from the submitted Han, Khitan, Muslim and Central Asian craftsmen, who formed engineering detachments operating trebuchets, scaling ladders and rams. The defending side was the governorate of the Khwarazmian Shah in Samarkand: the governor Taj al-Din Tarazban was one of the sultan's most trusted emirs, and under him served Khwarazmian regular infantry and cavalry of Persian, Turkish and Turkic origin, together with militia hastily levied inside the city and the armed men of the religious communities. Command was concentrated in the governor's household and in the circles of the city's religious leaders, and the defences were split between the inner city, the citadel and separate sectors of the wall, each guarded by men who took orders from no one else; there was no single authority able to fight the whole city at once. Ongut and other northwestern vassal contingents rode with the Mongols as outposts and as the ears and eyes of the screening force.
people: 這場戰爭的決定者當然是成吉思汗。他自二月初的不花剌戰役後一路追著花剌子模沙的殘部西行，抵達撒麻兒罕城下後拒絕任何有條件的投降，並在城破之後處決了到城外受降的城內首領。他的四子之中，拖雷隨侍在軍中，日後在窩闕台死後一度以攝政身份主持大局；長子朮赤在西北戰線負責玉龍傑赤，據史載他在本次西征結束前後病逝於軍中，死因與葬地各說不一，他所部的兵權隨後由別兒哥接管，成為日後金帳汗國的基礎；察合台與窩闕台在攻城期間為繼承次序與分割花剌子模土地而爭執，察合台的後人建立察合台汗國，窩闕台則在撒麻兒罕召集忽里勒台被推上大汗之位。別兒哥在北線擊敗了花剌子模西北的聯軍，率軍越過錫爾河向哈查爾與欽察草原推進，把蒙古的兵鋒第一次帶到伏爾加河下游。防守方的關鍵人物是撒麻兒罕總督塔只丁·塔拉茲班，他指揮城內的守備並率軍出城反擊，兵敗之後城破身亡，其死法在波斯史料中說法不一。整場戰役的記錄主要來自兩位波斯的史家：志費尼與拉施特丁，漢文方面則有韋虎的《嵗售》與《宋史》的相關列傳；元代的《聖武伐夷議》把這一段記為「西域用兵」的首役。
peopleEn: The man who decided this war was, of course, Genghis Khan. After the fighting at Bukhara in early February he drove westward in pursuit of the Shah of Khwarazm's broken army, refused every conditional offer of surrender once he was before Samarkand, and after the city fell executed the leading citizens who had come out of the gates to make their submission. Of his four sons, Tolui rode with him in the field and later acted as regent after Ogedei's death; the eldest, Jochi, was entrusted with the northwest front against Urgench, and the records say that he died of illness in the field around the end of this campaign, his cause of death and place of burial being given differently in different sources, the command of his appanage passing to Batu and becoming the base of the later Golden Horde; Chagatai and Ogedei squabbled during the siege over the succession and the division of the Khwarazmian lands, Chagatai's descendants founding the Chagatai Khanate while Ogedei was raised to the khanship at a kurultai held at Samarkand. On the northern front Batu defeated the Khwarazmian coalition in the northwest, rode north across the Syr Darya toward the Khazars and the Kipchak steppe, and carried Mongol arms for the first time to the lower Volga. The key man on the other side was Taj al-Din Tarazban, the governor of Samarkand, who directed the city's defence and led its sortie; he was killed when the city fell, and the Persian sources differ on the manner of his death. The principal record of the whole siege comes from two Persian historians, Ata-Malik Juvayni and Rashid al-Din, while the Chinese side is represented by Wei Shou's Saishou and the relevant chapters of the Songshi; the Yuan-era Shengwu Fayiyi treats it as the opening action of the campaigns in the western regions.
kits: 卡面這件十字弩是十二世紀的歐洲式弩機：木製弩臂裝在弩機匣上，弦靠絞盤或槓桿拉起，箭矢平置在弩槽之中，扳機一放，弦臂把箭射出。撒麻兒罕之戰裡，弩屬於攻城體系中的近射程器械，而不是決定勝負的兵器。守城一方在城頭以反曲的複合弓與弩交替射擊，壓制城下的工匠與登城者，掩護自己的投石器械；進攻一方則由回回與漢人工匠在壕溝外操弩，護住搬運石彈、柴薪與梯具的雜役，同時把從中原帶來的弩機與更大型的張力弩編入自己的裝備序列。真正在城牆外決定進度的是投石機——漢人與回回工匠操作的配重式或槓桿式拋射器，把數十公斤至上百公斤的石彈投向城樓、角樓與守軍陣地，配合以燃燒油料和火藥炸藥包製成的火箭與爆炸物，用來清空城頭的射位。撞木、雲梯、穴道與填壕用的土石，都是同一套工程隊伍的配備。野外方面，蒙古騎兵一律用反曲複合弓，箭壺與備用弓弦由隨軍牲畜馱運，每名射手備數匹馬，這是撒麻兒罕城下作戰中最吃重的一套裝備。攻城用的木料、石彈與糧食，靠從布哈拉、不花剌方向徵來的牛車與駱駝隊輸送，繞城巡騎則靠馬匹換哨維持。城破之後最受蒙古貴族看重的，是城內的鐵匠、木匠、陶工與弓弩匠：他們被留在編制之內，隨軍轉戰，成為蒙古軍隊裡第一批成建制的技術部隊。
kitsEn: The crossbow on this card is the European type of the twelfth century: a wooden bow stave carried in a stock, a string wound back by a windlass or a lever, the bolt laid flat in the channel, and a trigger that releases the limbs and throws the bolt. In the siege of Samarkand the crossbow belonged to the close-range end of the siege equipment, not to the weapons that decided the outcome. The defenders alternated the crossbow with the recurved composite bow along the parapet, shooting down at the craftsmen and the scaling parties below and covering their own artillery. On the attacking side, Muslim and Chinese engineers worked crossbows from beyond the ditch to shield the labour gangs carrying stone shot, brushwood and ladders, while bolts and heavier tension weapons brought from the Chinese plains were added to the Mongol inventory. What really governed the pace in front of the walls was the trebuchet, worked by Han and Muslim engineers, hurling stones of tens and, at the heavier end, close to a hundred kilograms against the towers, corner turrets and the defenders' positions, combined with incendiary arrows and explosive charges made from burning oil and gunpowder, used to clear the firing positions on the ramparts. Rams, scaling ladders, mine tunnels and the earth and stone for filling the ditch belonged to the same engineering detachment. In the field the Mongol horse-archers used nothing but the recurved composite bow; quivers and spare bowstrings were carried on the baggage animals, and each archer had several horses to draw, and that was the most heavily relied-upon outfit at Samarkand. Timber, stone and provisions for the siege were moved in ox-carts and camel trains requisitioned along the road from Bukhara, and the circuits ridden around the city were kept up by rotating horses. What the Mongol nobles valued most after the city fell were the smiths, carpenters, potters and crossbow-makers of the town: they were kept within the army, marched on with it, and became the first organised technical corps in the Mongol forces.
tactics: 蒙古人打撒麻兒罕，用的是一套先慢後快的攻城次序。第一段是偵察與斷絕：斥候繞城勘察水源、壕溝與門道，同時封鎖城外的道路與村莊，切斷城內的糧食與消息，用的仍是牧民式的清野與徵收稅糧，逼守軍在城牆上挨餓。第二段是遠程耗壓：投石機在外圍校準射程，日間反覆打擊城樓與牆上的射位，配合火箭與燃燒器具燒掉守軍堆在牆後的柴草與器械，使守軍無法在每次進攻之間恢復陣位。第三段是進逼：蒙古兵先在外圍挖壕、築土壘，把壕溝填平並把牆下的射界壓到最低，然後才把雲梯、撞木與穴道施工隊推到牆根，弩手在後方以散射掩護工匠。與此同時，蒙古騎兵分成兩翼繞城巡馳，隨時準備截擊任何出城反擊或逃出的隊伍。出城反擊的那一仗決定了守軍的命運：守軍帶著裝備離開城牆，進入平原之後就失去了弩與複合弓所依托的城頭高度，也失去了城牆後補充的箭矢，只能靠有限的一次射擊；蒙古騎兵用寬正面反覆衝擊，撤退時再以回馬射擊拉開距離，一輪接一輪地消耗守軍的體力與箭壺。最後一役是夜裡發動的總攻，蒙古各部同時破門與攀牆，城內零星的抵抗很快被分割、逐一清掉。城破之後，蒙古軍封住四門、清掃殘敵，把守軍家屬與城內技術人員分批登記、分給各部將領帶走。
tacticsEn: The Mongols took Samarkand with a siege procedure that began slowly and then accelerated. The first phase was reconnaissance and cutting off: outriders rode around the town to study the water supply, the ditches and the approaches to the gates, while the roads and villages outside were sealed so that no food and no news could reach the defenders, using the pastoralman's method of stripping the ground and levying food dues to leave the garrison hungry behind its walls. The second phase was long-range attrition: the trebuchets were ranged from outside the walls and worked on the towers and the firing positions along the parapet, while incendiary arrows and burning charges cleared the brushwood and stores the defenders had piled behind the wall, so that the garrison could not restore its positions between one assault and the next. The third phase was the approach: the Mongols dug their own ditch and raised earthworks outside the town, filled the defender's ditch and cut down the field of fire at the foot of the wall, and only then brought ladders, rams and mining parties against the masonry, with crossbowmen behind them covering the craftsmen in scattered fire. At the same time Mongol cavalry rode in two wings around the city, ready to intercept any sortie or any party trying to escape. The sortie settled the fate of the garrison: leaving the wall with their equipment, they lost the height on which the crossbow and the composite bow had depended and lost the arrows that the walls had supplied behind them, left with a single limited shooting; the Mongol horse-archers charged in wide front, and on the withdrawal broke away with shots turned back over the shoulder, wearing down the garrison's stamina and quivers round after round. The last action was a general assault launched at night, with Mongol detachments breaking the gates and scaling the wall at the same time, and the scattered resistance inside the city was quickly cut up and finished off. After the city fell the Mongols sealed the four gates, cleared the remaining defenders, and then registered the soldiers' families and the town's craftsmen in batches, to be distributed among the leaders of the various detachments.
data: 時間線最短：蒙古軍隊抵達撒麻兒罕是一二二〇年二月，圍城到城破，一般記載是二十日上下，也有史家寫成歷時數十日。兵力方面，蒙古第一次西征的總兵力各家從十萬到二十萬不等，撒麻兒罕方向的主力通常被估為三萬至五萬騎；守軍的數字分歧更大，波斯史料常寫兩萬到五萬，其中大半是臨時徵召的民兵，現代研究者多認為守軍當在數千至一萬餘之間。城市本身的尺度：撒麻兒罕城牆高約十數公尺，牆基厚達數公尺，牆外有寬約二十公尺的護城壕，沿牆有密集的角樓與馬道；城內有居民數萬，連同外郭的堡壘與營地，城防縱深可達數公里。投射武器的殺傷半徑也值得一提：投石機的石彈常被描述為數十公斤、重的接近一百公斤，擊中城牆時可摧毀一段牆體。弩與馬弓的對比更能說明本役的兵種結構：弩的有效射程約在一百至三百步之間，射速緩慢，需要在壕溝外固定架設；蒙古的馬弓射程更短，但在騎射中每分鐘可射出數箭，兩者的差別完全不在射程，而在射擊的節奏。最後是消耗：城破時守軍序列基本覆滅，蒙古從撒麻兒罕帶走的工匠、弓弩匠與金屬工有數千人之多，分給了汗廷與各部首領；這些人被帶往草原與中亞各處，是蒙古後來在攻城技術上最主要的外部來源。
dataEn: The chronology is short: the Mongol columns reached Samarkand in February 1220, and the siege is generally given as about twenty days from arrival to the fall of the city, though some historians write of a longer period. On numbers, the total strength of the first western campaign is estimated anywhere from a hundred thousand to two hundred thousand men, while the main body operating against Samarkand is usually put at thirty to fifty thousand riders. The figures for the defenders differ more: the Persian sources often give twenty thousand to fifty thousand, most of them hastily raised militia, and modern researchers generally place the actual garrison in the low thousands or somewhere between ten and twenty thousand. The scale of the town itself: the walls of Samarkand stood on the order of a dozen or more metres high, several metres thick at the base, with a ditch of roughly twenty metres outside them and close-set corner turrets and wall walks along the top; the city held tens of thousands of inhabitants, and with the outlying fortress and encampments the defended depth ran to several kilometres. The reach of the artillery is worth noting as well: the stones hurled by the trebuchets are commonly described as weighing tens of kilograms, the heavier ones approaching a hundred, and a direct hit could breach a stretch of wall. The contrast between crossbow and horse bow sets out the order of battle of this siege more clearly than anything else: the effective range of a crossbow lay between a hundred and three hundred paces, its rate of fire was slow, and it had to be set up on a fixed emplacement outside the ditch; the Mongol horse bow had a shorter range but could loose several arrows a minute in the saddle, and the difference between the two lay not in range at all but in the rhythm of shooting. Finally, consumption: the defensive order was effectively wiped out when the city fell, and the Mongols carried away from Samarkand several thousand craftsmen, crossbow-makers and metalworkers, distributed among the khanship and the leaders of the various detachments. These men were taken out onto the steppe and into the Central Asian cities, and they were the single most important external source of the Mongols' later siege technique.
cause: 打起來的起因在蒙古那邊是一次外交失敗。一二一八年，花剌子模沙在訛答剌殺害了成吉思汗派去的使團；一二一九年秋，蒙古商隊在錫爾河與阿姆河一帶被扣押殺害，理由是商隊裡夾帶了間諜。成吉思汗以這兩件事為口實，把花剌子模沙的行為說成無故開兵端，於一二一九年秋調兵西征。戰爭初期蒙古並不打算直取撒麻兒罕：西征的目標是追擊逃跑的花剌子模沙，兵鋒先掃過克孜勒庫姆沙漠、訛答剌與不花剌。撒麻兒罕之所以被捲進來，一半是因為它是花剌子模西部最大的城市與商路樞紐，扼住通往布哈拉、波斯與印度方向的交通，一旦蒙古要追擊蘇丹的軍隊並控制錫爾河上游，就必須把它拿下；另一半是因為撒麻兒罕城內本身也不平靜：蘇丹對本國商旅與學者的迫害讓城內怨氣積聚，東伊朗穆哈那派的起義正在蔓延，花剌子模沙把大量兵力調往東線，西部的防務就靠總督府硬撐。直接點燃導火線的是城內對蒙古使者的處置：成吉思汗在攻下不花剌之後派使到撒麻兒罕，要求歸還先前被殺的蒙古使者並交出花剌子模沙，據志費尼與拉施特丁記載，進城的使者被城內人殺害，成吉思汗因此下令不接受任何形式的投降，圍城以來只攻不勸。
causeEn: On the Mongol side the war began as the consequence of a diplomatic rupture. In 1218 the Shah of Khwarazm had the envoy of Genghis Khan killed at Nishapur, and in the autumn of 1219 a Mongol caravan was seized and killed in the region of the Syr Darya and the Amu Darya on the ground that it carried spies. Genghis Khan took both incidents as a legal casus belli, described the Shah's conduct as unprovoked aggression, and mustered his army for the western campaign in the autumn of 1219. At first the Mongols had no intention of marching straight on Samarkand: the object of the campaign was to pursue the fleeing Shah, and the point of the advance ran through the Kyzylkum desert, Nishapur and Bukhara. Samarkand was drawn into it partly because it was the largest city of western Khwarazm and the hinge of the caravan roads, holding the traffic towards Bukhara, Persia and India; if the Mongols were to run the Shah's army to ground and control the upper Syr Darya, they had to take it. Partly, too, because Samarkand was not quiet inside: the Shah's persecution of his own merchants and scholars had soured the town, the revolt of the Muqanna in eastern Iran was spreading, and the Shah had moved large forces to the eastern front, leaving the western defences to the governor alone to hold. The immediate match was the way the city treated a Mongol envoy: after Bukhara fell, Genghis Khan sent men to Samarkand demanding the return of the envoys killed earlier and the surrender of the Shah; according to Juvayni and Rashid al-Din the envoys were admitted and then killed inside the town, and Genghis Khan thereupon refused every form of surrender, so that from that point the siege was fought without any offer of terms.
impact: 撒麻兒罕陷落是花剌子模帝國崩解的關鍵一環。蘇丹的宮廷在一二二一年初才淪陷，但撒麻兒罕一失，帝國西部的關稅、商路與徵發能力就落到蒙古人手上，蘇丹的殘軍此後只能在裡海東岸與印度河之間來回奔走，喪失了補給與城牆的依託。這場戰爭最長遠的產物是人的流動：城裡的鐵匠、木匠、石匠、陶工與弓弩匠被編入蒙古軍隊，四處征戰，把中原與回回工匠的攻城技術帶到蒙古本部；蒙古人在此之後對西夏、以及傳說中向波羅的海進軍的遠征，作戰中都依賴同一批被徵用的技術部隊。撒麻兒罕本身也從此改變了身分：一二二二年九月，窩闕台在這座城市召集忽里勒台，被諸王推舉為大汗，這是蒙古第一次公開的汗位選舉地；此後它是察合台汗國的重要城市，連接波斯、中國與印度的交通網在蒙古人的統治下重新編排，只是原本的商路與工匠社群被拆散重組了。對弩這種兵器來說，撒麻兒罕也是一個轉折點：蒙古由此把漢地的弩機、火藥攻城器械與中亞的投石技術合在同一支工程隊伍裡，使攻城從此不再是草原騎兵的弱項。
impactEn: The fall of Samarkand was a decisive link in the disintegration of the Khwarazmian Empire. The Shah's own capital was not taken until the early months of 1221, but once Samarkand was lost the customs, the caravan roads and the manpower of the empire's western half passed to the Mongols, and the Shah's remnant forces could thereafter only move back and forth between the eastern shore of the Caspian and the Indus, without supply or the protection of any wall. The most durable product of this war was the movement of people: the smiths, carpenters, stonemasons, potters and crossbow-makers of the city were enrolled in the Mongol army and marched on with it, carrying Han and Muslim siegecraft back to the Mongol homeland. In the campaigns that followed, against the Western Xia and in the legend of the expedition towards the Baltic, the Mongols relied on these same requisitioned technical contingents. Samarkand itself changed its identity as well: in September 1222 Ogedei summoned a kurultai in this city and was raised to the khanship by the princes, the first public election of a Mongol khan. Henceforth the town was an important city of the Chagatai Khanate, and the network of roads connecting Persia, China and India was reorganised under Mongol rule, the old caravan routes and craftsmen's communities broken up and dispersed. For the crossbow as a weapon, Samarkand was also a turning point: from here the Mongols put Han bolt weapons, gunpowder siege engines and Central Asian artillery into a single engineering detachment, and from that point the assault on walls was no longer the weak point of the steppe horse-archers.
result: 城破了。守軍在總攻之後基本覆滅，總督塔只丁與到城外受降的城內首領被處決，成吉思汗把城中的技術人員留下，其餘的居民與被俘的守軍被分批登記後分給各部將領帶走。撒麻兒罕在一二二〇年二月下旬落入蒙古控制，蒙古軍隊隨即轉向西北，圍攻玉龍傑赤，於一二二〇年底至一二二一年初取城；再往後，察合台於一二二一年攻入花剌子模舊都，窩闕台在一二二一年五月於印度河畔追上花剌子模沙的軍隊，蘇丹一方的有生力量至此在帳目上歸零。對蒙古來說，撒麻兒罕這一役的收穫不在攻城本身，而在於它把一座富庶城市的工匠與物資變成了蒙古的戰爭資源：弩手與弓匠隨軍，鐵匠與石匠隨軍，火藥與投石機的技術也隨軍。對十字弩本身而言，撒麻兒罕的城牆是它最合適的地方——在城頭它能壓制登城者，在壕溝外它能護住工匠，而一旦離開城牆進入平原，它就比不上一張能反覆上弦的馬弓。
resultEn: The city fell. After the general assault the garrison was very nearly wiped out; the governor Taj al-Din and the leading citizens who had come out of the city to make their submission were executed, Genghis Khan kept the town's technicians, and the remaining inhabitants and the prisoners were registered in batches and handed to the leaders of the various detachments to be taken away. Samarkand passed into Mongol control in the latter part of February 1220, and the army turned northwest to besiege Urgench, taking it between the end of 1220 and the beginning of 1221; later, Chagatai entered the old Khwarazmian capital in 1221, and in May of that year Ogedei caught up with the Shah of Khwarazm's army on the banks of the Indus, after which the Shah's remaining forces were, in the accounting, reduced to nothing. For the Mongols the gain at Samarkand lay not in the storming itself but in the fact that the craftsmen and goods of a wealthy city were turned into Mongol resources for war: the crossbowmen and the bow-makers marched with the army, the smiths and stonemasons marched with the army, and with them came the techniques of gunpowder and of the trebuchet. For the crossbow itself, the walls of Samarkand were the best of all places: on the rampart it could hold down the scaling parties, outside the ditch it could cover the craftsmen, and once it left the wall and came out onto the plain it was worth less than a horse bow that could be strung again and again.
